text:
support-liz: FYI - multiple customers reporting p99 spikes from EU region since ~09:03 UTC. Tickets show 1.2-1.8s p99 for API calls that normally sit ~200ms. Example req ids: req=abcd1234, req=ef56gh. Attaching curl/traceroute in thread.

oncall-bot: [alert] EU-pop p99 > 1s for 12m, affected services: inference-api, embeddings. Alert id: A-2026-4472 :rotating_light:

sre-jen: taking this. Initial triage: looks like a subset of traffic is being routed to a US pop (adds ~150-200ms). Can folks paste quick dig/mtr from a repro client? @netops-aaron can you check DNS shard mappings and recent changes?

netops-aaron: I see a small percentage (~4-6%) of queries for shard-1001.redwood.net resolving to 3.128.45.22 (us-west) instead of the normal eu IP 34.23.54.12. This started ~09:00 UTC. TTL on the eu record dropped to 0 briefly during a cloud DNS refresh (provider side), then oscillated. dig output sample:
```
$ dig +short shard-1001.redwood.net @8.8.8.8
34.23.54.12
3.128.45.22
```
and `dig shard-1001.redwood.net` shows TTL 30 -> 0 -> 30 flips in the last 5m.

support-liz: customer trace (from their lambda in eu-west-1):
```
mtr -r -c 10 api.redwood.net
1  10.1.0.1  1.2 ms
...
6  34.23.54.12  24 ms
7  3.128.45.22  180 ms  <-- cross-continent hop seen intermittently
```
and curl -w "time_starttransfer:%{time_starttransfer}\n" -o /dev/null -s -D - -X POST https://api.redwood.net/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer x"
response shows TLS handshake time ~0.150s and TTFB ~0.20-0.25s when hitting eu IP, but ~1.6-1.8s when request went to us-west.

sre-jen: repro steps I used:
```
# force client DNS to our resolver
dig +short shard-1001.redwood.net @1.1.1.1
# mimic client's route by pinning
curl --resolve api.redwood.net:443:34.23.54.12 https://api.redwood.net/health -v
# compare with us IP
curl --resolve api.redwood.net:443:3.128.45.22 https://api.redwood.net/health -v
```
When resolved to 3.128.45.22 handshake times ~160-200ms extra and occasionally fails TLS early-close (client retries create fanned p99).

prod-eng-maya: could TLS session resumption be part of it? If clients hit a different pop they renegotiate and lack cached session tickets -> added RTT. Also check if our edge LB is introducing extra hops when traffic lands in a non-local AZ.

netops-aaron: confirmed: session ticket cache is per-pop. So cross-pop resolution will cause full handshake. Cloud DNS refresh coincided with a maintenance window in the provider that briefly rotated shard assignments. That explains the intermittent flips.

sre-jen: short mitigation plan:
- Apply temporary route pin in edge config to prefer eu-pop for shard-1001 for 30m (rollback plan ready)
- Increase authoritative TTL for shard affinitized records to 300s to reduce flip rate (careful: TTL increase has delayed rollback cost)
- Adjust client fallback policy to try local-pop first and only fallback asynchronously (reduce sync retries)
- Communications: let affected customers know the root cause & workaround (support-liz)

support-liz: I've pushed a message to affected customers offering a short-term workaround: set header "x-redwood-region: eu" or use DNS override if possible. Logged in support tickets.

edge-bot: Applied route-pin: service=inference-api shard=1001 mode=eu-prefer ttl=1800 — change id CHG-8721 — will auto-revert in 30m unless approved.

sre-jen: monitoring after route-pin: p99 dropped from ~1.6s -> 0.24s within 2m. See dashboard link: https://console.redwood.net/dashboards/p99-eu (internal)

prod-eng-maya: +1 to TTL bump and route-pin. Also suggest adding a guard in our edge to prefer session-ticket warmup for new TLS endpoints after pop changes (ticket pre-warm) — filing JIRA: INF-5821.

netops-aaron: provider confirmed they rolled a DNS refresh that created transient multi-pop answers; asked them to avoid rotating shard-to-pop mapping during production windows. They're submitting a postmortem.

sre-jen: next steps: keep pinned for 30m, watch p99 and retries. If stable -> increase TTL and remove pin carefully. I'll create a short postmortem note once provider PM shares timeline. Leaving thread open for 60m for telemetry stabilization.

support-liz: customers updated. Closing customer-facing incident after 1 hour if metrics stay stable.

oncall-bot: [resolve] Alert A-2026-4472 set to resolved by operator: sre-jen — metrics within normal range. :white_check_mark:

sre-jen: follow-up: created brief postmortem draft and action items:
- INF-5821 (session-ticket warmup)
- NET-3173 (DNS shard TTL defaults and provider gating)
- DOCS-120 (support KB: region header workaround)

sre-jen: thanks everyone. Reopen if we see recurrence.
